editorial:
Imagine you and your college friends heading into the Norwegian woods with a camera, thinking you are just filming a school project about dead bears. That is exactly how you enter this story. You follow a group of students who stumble upon something way weirder than they expected. They find a grumpy guy who spends his days hunting massive, ugly trolls that the government tries to keep a secret. The whole thing feels like a home video or a news report, which makes the monsters feel way more real. It is a wild ride that mixes a bit of scary tension with some funny moments as the kids realize they are in over their heads.

What really makes this work is how the trolls look and act. They are not your typical fairy tale creatures; they are huge, gross, and dangerous. The pacing is great because it starts slow and then turns into a total nightmare. If you like movies that feel like a discovery, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a scary way. The students get trapped in a cave with a giant troll. While they try to escape, the monster catches up to them. You see the camera drop as the troll attacks, meaning the students do not make it out alive. The footage they recorded is the only thing that survives, showing the world that trolls are real and the government has been lying about them the whole time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster movies and shaky-cam style stories.
